advisory.description: n8n before 1.123.67, 2.x before 2.31.5, and 2.32.x before 2.32.1 contain a type confusion vulnerability in the Send Email node, which does not enforce that its message fields are strings. A crafted non-string value supplied from a workflow expression into the text or HTML body field can be interpreted by the underlying mail library (Nodemailer) as a file path or URL, allowing arbitrary local file disclosure and server-side request forgery (SSRF). Exploitation requires a pre-existing active workflow with an unauthenticated webhook, valid SMTP credentials configured on the node, and untrusted input mapped directly into the body field; this is not a default configuration.

cwes.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

same_repository_prior_hits.mechanism: Credential authorization bypass: pre-execution CredentialsPermissionChecker trusts the unresolved literal of the genericAuthType parameter (which may be an expression) when filtering active credential types, so the ownership/access check is skipped and the attacker-referenced credential is loaded at execution time. An authenticated member with edit access to a shared workflow can reference another user's credential in the HTTP Request node, exfiltrate/use it.

Git node fetch/pull/pushTags operations bypass sandbox path restriction: repository-path containment checks (assertRepositoryReferenceAllowed) protect clone and push, but fetch/pull/pushTags lack them, so an authenticated user with workflow create/execute rights can point an allowlisted remote config value at a local path outside the intended sandbox, pull an arbitrary local git repo into the workspace, and read its files/history.

Git node clone TOCTOU: repositoryPath resolved (resolvePathAllowingMissingParents) and checked (isFilePathBlocked), then mkdir(dirname(resolvedRepositoryPath)) and git.clone(sourceRepository, resolvedRepositoryPath) run later; an authenticated user can swap a validated directory for a symlink in the window before the clone subprocess runs, so git writes a crafted repo into the community-node directory which n8n loads as custom nodes on restart -> RCE.

XML node prototype-pollution patch bypass: the GHSA-hqr4-h3xv-9m3r patch validated `String(options.attrkey ?? '')` / charkey against forbidden keys but forwarded the raw (uncoerced) options object to xml2js Parser/Builder; a stateful non-string value (toString() returning a safe string on first call, attacker key on later calls) passes validation yet coerces to __proto__/constructor when the parser uses it, restoring prototype pollution -> RCE.

External Secrets permission bypass caused by parser mismatch: credential validation detected only tightly formatted $secrets expressions, while the runtime expression engine accepted whitespace/newline variants, allowing users without externalSecret:list to store references that later resolved to protected secret values.

The JavaScript Code node executes user code in the task-runner Node VM with host objects injected into the sandbox. `$input.constructor.constructor.prototype` is the host Function.prototype. The freeze loop only froze prototypes with `typeof === 'object'`, but `typeof Function.prototype === 'function'`, so that prototype stayed mutable. An authenticated user who can create and execute workflows can pollute Function.prototype, recover host globalThis, and complete a sandbox escape when allowlisted imports (NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN / NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL) supply gadgets. CWE-1321. Patched in 1.123.69, 2.33.4, and 2.34.1 by freezing function-typed prototypes as well (`isFreezable` = object or function).

Path traversal reaches dynamic require. CNA metadata says 2.0.0, but Git containment first proves the unsafe loader carrier in n8n@2.9.0 and the advisory-specific MCP source-to-sink in n8n@2.25.1; n8n@2.33.3 and n8n@2.34.0 are verified affected endpoints.

context_rule: One case, one clean context. Do not read the canonical ledger, another case bundle/output, or a prior verdict. Prior hits are leads, never proof.
